# Results — Study 211 (Sin-Stocks)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Equal-weight sin basket
(MO, PM, STZ, LVS, LMT, RTX) vs SPY (SPDR S&P 500 ETF) and DSI (iShares MSCI KLD 400
Social ETF), daily adjusted total-return closes, 2008-03-18 to 2026-06-12 (n = 4,589
trading days ≈ 18.2 years).  Alignment starts at PM's spin-out date 2008-03-17 (inner join).
All prices are `auto_adjust=True` from Yahoo Finance via yfinance.
As-of **2026-06-12**.*

The sin basket is equally weighted across six tickers spanning tobacco (MO, PM), alcohol/beer
(STZ), gambling (LVS), and defense (LMT, RTX).  Equal weighting avoids the concentration
bias of a market-cap-weighted construction but implies daily rebalancing.
`auto_adjust=True` ensures dividends are included — critical for tobacco and defense stocks,
which are high-yield dividend payers; unadjusted prices would severely understate their
total return.

## Headline: sin basket vs benchmarks

| Metric | SIN_EW | SPY | DSI (ESG) | SIN winner? |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| **CAGR** | **+10.60%** | **+12.17%** | **+12.11%** | No — lagged both |
| Annualised vol | 20.9% | 19.8% | 19.8% | SPY/DSI (lower vol) |
| **Sharpe (gross, rf=0)** | **+0.481** | **+0.579** | **+0.577** | **No** |
| Max drawdown | −65.9% | −51.5% | −49.9% | SPY/DSI (shallower) |
| Total return since 2008-03 | **527%** | **710%** | **702%** | **No** |

The sin basket lagged the S&P 500 by **−1.57 pp/yr in CAGR** and had a **Sharpe ratio
0.098 lower** despite nominally comparable volatility.  Its maximum drawdown (−65.9%, driven
mainly by LVS which fell −98.3% peak-to-trough) far exceeded both benchmarks.

## The honest signal test — excess return vs SPY

### Excess return (SIN_EW − SPY daily log-return)

| Metric | Value |
|---|--:|
| Mean excess return | **−0.56 bps/day** |
| Annualised CAGR differential | **−1.40%/yr** |
| HAC *t*-stat (Newey-West) | **−0.46** |
| Excess-return Sharpe 95% CI | **[−0.539, +0.339]** |
| Bootstrap resamples with negative excess Sharpe | **68%** |

The excess return is **−1.40%/yr** with a HAC *t* of **−0.46** — far below the |*t*| = 2
inference bar.  The neglect premium hypothesis predicts a positive excess return; the data
show the opposite sign with no statistical support.  The bootstrap 95% CI
([−0.539, +0.339]) straddles zero, with 68% of resamples negative.

### OLS alpha / beta decomposition

The neglect premium claim predicts a positive market-neutral alpha.  OLS regression of
SIN_EW daily log-returns on SPY daily log-returns:

| Coefficient | Value | *t*-stat |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Alpha (daily)** | **+0.242 bps/day** | **+0.20** |
| Alpha (annualised) | **+0.61%/yr** | — |
| **Beta** | **0.825** | — |
| R² | 0.609 | — |

Beta = 0.825 reflects the tobacco/defense/alcohol sector tilt away from high-beta tech
(notably absent from all six tickers).  The OLS alpha is +0.242 bps/day (+0.61%/yr) with
*t* = +0.20 — statistically indistinguishable from zero.  There is **no evidence of a
market-neutral neglect premium** in this sample; the gross underperformance is explained by
a combination of lower beta (which reduces upside in bull markets) and idiosyncratic drag
from the LVS casino stock.

### SIN_EW vs DSI (ESG ETF)

| Coefficient | Value | *t*-stat |
|---|--:|--:|
| Alpha (daily) | +0.444 bps/day | +0.34 |
| Alpha (annualised) | +1.13%/yr | — |
| Beta | 0.784 | — |
| R² | 0.550 | — |

The comparison with DSI (the ESG counter-portfolio) mirrors the SPY result: the alpha is
positive in point estimate but completely insignificant (t = +0.34).

## Per-ticker attribution — the basket is not broad-based

| Ticker | Sector | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe | Max DD |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| MO  | Tobacco (US) | +13.64% | 21.8% | 0.59 | −53.7% |
| PM  | Tobacco (Intl) | +12.57% | 23.6% | 0.50 | −42.9% |
| STZ | Alcohol/Beer | +13.35% | 30.0% | 0.42 | −53.5% |
| LVS | Gambling/Casinos | **+0.62%** | **58.5%** | **0.01** | **−98.3%** |
| LMT | Defense | +13.09% | 23.7% | 0.52 | −50.6% |
| RTX | Defense | +10.95% | 26.7% | 0.39 | −52.0% |

LVS (Las Vegas Sands) is the critical outlier: near-zero CAGR, vol of 58.5%, and a −98.3%
peak-to-trough drawdown (reflecting the pandemic casino shutdown plus Macau regulatory risk).
The other five tickers — tobacco and defense — delivered reasonable returns (CAGR +10.95% to
+13.64%) with Sharpe ratios 0.39–0.59.  Without LVS, the basket CAGR would be approximately
+12.72% with excess return approximately +0.49%/yr (still insignificant).  The "sin" label
bundles defensible income stocks (tobacco, defense) with a speculative casino play.

## Crash behavior — mixed protection record

SPY drawdown episodes >= 10%:

| Episode | SPY max DD | SPY total ret | SIN_EW total ret | Protection |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| GFC 2008–2011 | −51.5% | +12.3% | +23.9% | **+11.7 pp** |
| 2011 correction | −18.6% | +13.2% | +17.4% | **+4.3 pp** |
| 2015–2016 correction | −13.0% | +12.2% | +23.1% | **+10.9 pp** |
| Feb 2018 VIX shock | −10.1% | +11.4% | −2.2% | **−13.6 pp** |
| Dec 2018 bear | −19.3% | +12.5% | +11.7% | **−0.9 pp** |
| COVID crash 2020 | −33.7% | +14.0% | −5.4% | **−19.4 pp** |
| 2022 bear market | −24.5% | +12.5% | +4.3% | **−8.3 pp** |
| Apr 2025 tariff shock | −18.8% | +11.6% | +4.0% | **−7.7 pp** |

Protection is **mixed**: positive in the early period (2008–2016) and negative in the
growth-led bear markets (2018–2025).  The pattern matches a value/defensives tilt: sin stocks
act as a buffer when market stress is recession-driven (where tobacco, beer, and defense
maintain demand), but underperform when stress is liquidity-driven (COVID) or rate-driven
(2022).

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Excess-return HAC *t* = −0.46 vs SPY and −0.42 vs DSI (wrong sign,
  far below |t| = 2).  OLS alpha is +0.61%/yr (t = +0.20): statistically indistinguishable
  from zero.  The Hong-Kacperczyk neglect premium is not confirmed in this basket over this
  post-publication sample.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Lower CAGR (−1.57 pp vs SPY), lower Sharpe (0.481 vs 0.579),
  worse max drawdown (−65.9% vs −51.5%) than both SPY and DSI.  LVS wrecks the basket.
  Daily rebalancing across 6 stocks adds implementation friction.
- **Crash shield (myth-check) — MIXED.** Protected in 3 of 8 episodes (GFC era), failed in
  5 of the 8 episodes (post-2018).  The regime-dependence makes it unreliable as a defensive
  overlay.
